status: Protocol fixed before ensemble execution; exploratory model study, not a real-water validation
question: Does one mass-only D2O substitution alter organization or intervention-defined response in a confined explicit classical water model?
model: OpenMM 8.6.1 rigid TIP3P; nonperiodic all-pairs Coulomb and oxygen Lennard-Jones, no cutoff; same charges, geometry and potential in all arms
boundary: Oxygen-only spherical flat-bottom wall: 0.5*10000*max(0,r-R)^2 kJ/mol; R=0.4 nm for N=9, scales as N^(1/3); wall sensitivity R=0.5 nm
temperature: 300 K LangevinMiddle, friction 1/ps; 0.1/ps sensitivity; 1 fs step, 0.5 fs sensitivity; rigid constraints 1e-8; no COM remover
main: 16 independently randomized nonoverlapping initial configurations, each with 2 velocity/thermostat seeds; A plus D at each of 9 initial radial-rank sites plus a label-only control; 50 ps equilibration, 100 ps production; all sites retained without outcome selection
label_control: Identical A simulation and random renaming/reordering of molecule IDs in saved analysis rows; same physical masses, positions, force evaluation and random numbers. Separate force/short NVE whole-molecule permutation test.
sensitivity: Long: 8 configs x 2 seeds x A/D0/D8, 100+300 ps; N=27: 8x2xA/D0/D26, 100+100 ps; radius: 8x2xA/D0/D8, 50+100 ps; half timestep and reduced friction: each 4x2xA/D0/D8, 50+100 ps. N=27 one substitution changes concentration, so finite size and dilution are confounded.
sampling: Coordinates and potential/kinetic energies every 0.05 ps, equilibration energies every 1 ps; three response snapshots at 25%, 50%, 75% production
hydrogen_bond: Directed O-O <0.35 nm and D-H-A angle >=150 deg for either donor H; network is undirected union, no chemical bond breaking
organization: early/late degree-rank correlation and top-occupancy with ties split
dynamics: nearest oxygen neighbor identity changes per molecule per ps (PRIMARY dynamical)
new H-bond episode lifetime Kaplan-Meier restricted mean to 2 ps, exclude left-censored episodes and retain right censoring
oxygen-neighbor residence KM restricted mean to 2 ps
response: At each snapshot, source molecule receives +/-0.05 dalton nm/ps total momentum along each Cartesian axis, distributed as common velocity to its atoms. Run paired deterministic NVE branches for lags 0, 0.02, 0.1, 0.5 ps. R_ij(lag)=sqrt(mean_axes ||[r_j(+J)-r_j(-J)]/(2J)||^2); target is oxygen; remove diagonal for transmitted influence. PRIMARY response is mean off-diagonal R at 0.5 ps. No first-mover inference. Equal impulse, not equal injected energy; amplitude and timestep checks included.
local_collective: Compare tagged-node degree, untagged-to-untagged H-bond degree, response to targets initially farther than 0.35 nm, and effective response participation; transient propagation does not establish a persistent leader.
inference: Paired differences within config/velocity; average positions then velocity seeds for mass main effects; resample entire initial-configuration clusters (10000 bootstrap samples). Report raw difference, 95% percentile CI, cluster paired standardized effect dz, sign-flip p with Holm across 3 primary outcomes. Secondary intervals unadjusted exploratory. Frames and molecules never treated as independent replicates.
interaction: Group D(inner)-D(outer), and tagged-node [D0-A0]-[Dlast-Alast]; initial position is an initial condition that can be forgotten after equilibration, not a fixed spatial location.
theory: For separable classical kinetic energy and fixed mass-independent potential, equilibrium configurational probabilities are mass independent. Independent rigid-body orientation integration also gives a mass-dependent constant that cancels within each composition. Finite-time structural differences are expected sampling/integration/equilibration diagnostics, not proof of classical isotope-dependent equilibrium structure.
limits: Confined few-molecule model, TIP3P limitations, no nuclear quantum/vibrational physics, no isotope exchange chemistry, no bulk extrapolation, no NS claim or inference about evolution of water over geological time. D2O total molecular mass is about 11.2% larger, not an infinitesimal change. No claim of statistical equivalence or real-water null result.
